title: Aluminium Alloy Side Link Fitting at the Fwd Engine Mount
abstract: The forward engine mount side link fitting is machined from aluminium alloy plate with an interference-fit bush at the lug bore and an increased lug edge distance, to arrest the fretting found at entry into service.

sections.reason: Entry-into-service experience showed fretting at the side link lug bore of the forward engine mount on aircraft flown at high thrust derates with frequent short sectors. Eight fittings were removed in the first eighteen months of operation, three of them at unscheduled events. The original bush retention relied on an adhesive bond that was not surviving the thermal cycle, and this modification introduced an interference-fit bush together with a revised lug edge distance.
sections.description: The forward mount side link fitting is machined from aluminium alloy plate with an interference-fit bush at the lug bore and a 3 mm increase in lug edge distance. The frame kit D5450125251057 that carries the fitting into the pylon primary structure is retained, and the rib D5450126830111 is re-shimmed to hold the revised link geometry. Attachment is with countersunk screws AES177340K7 to the torque schedule of the pylon standard practice. General arrangement is on drawing D54500067607. Access is through the pylon fairings in zones 431 and 441 with the engine removed. The bush is cold-expanded into the bore on a bench rather than in situ, which is why the fitting is supplied as a completed assembly.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 1.4 kg per pylon. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable with the pre-modification fitting because the lug bore diameter and the bush interference differ. A life limit of 24 000 flight cycles is attached to the fitting and has to be tracked separately from the pylon. A strip inspection of the lug bore is required at every engine shop visit, which became the principal operator complaint against this standard.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through Service Bulletin MRD-54-1019. This standard is not cut into the production line: the pylon join sequence cannot absorb the bench cold-expansion of the bush, so the fitting is supplied as a completed assembly and installed at an engine removal. Typical embodiment is two days per pylon with the engine already off the wing.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric across both pylons, no reportable CG shift
type_data.production_impact: Retrofit standard only, never cut in as a production solution

title: Aluminium Alloy Side Link Fitting at the Fwd Engine Mount

issue.reason: Combined embodiment package with the mount sleeving change recorded, together with the requirement to re-measure the sleeve termination clearance against the fitting standard actually installed.
